main_text.p: caufam differentiæ pofitam, quæ eft voluntas Dei.v.18.contra objectionem cæcæ rationis, v.19. à potestate Figuli si-milí. Quid autem illi Græcæ & Latinæ Ecclesiæ Patres iidem? Non hoc (inquit Chrysosto-mus.Chrysostomus) dicit, tollens [illegible, ~10 letters] sed demonstrans, quousque parendum sit Deo. Nihil contra nos. Nam & nos fatemur: 1. non ideo similitudinem istam figuli Apostolum attulisse; ut tolleret differentiam hominum, & vasorum figuli: quæ est, in ratione illorum, de quibus primò agit; & irrationalitate horum, de quibus propter illos. 2. Ostendi ibi; quousque parendum sit Deo scilicet non responsare debere figmentum fictori: ut habent immediatè antecedentia, responsantis voluntati divinæ, pro arbitrio hujus miserenti, illum indurantí.
Neque inde efficitur tamen, hoc solum dici: & non etiam, prorsus nullam differentiam, cujus causa prævisa fit, statui; sed merę Dei voluntati adscribi.
»Deus enim est, qui discernit. 1 Cor. 4.v.7. Hinc certè nata erat objectionis importunitas,

page.notes: Left margin note reads "Chrysostomus" split across two lines with a hyphen. The Greek word after "tollens" is not legible enough to copy. Long s is printed as a form resembling f in places; transcribed as s. Word "pofitam" is printed as such (likely "politam" or "positam"); copied as seen with [?] not added because the printed form is clear enough to show the printer's spelling. The "»" mark beside the Deus line is a printed ornament in the margin.
